PullRequest.Title: sessions: show the editor of a session inside the Agents window
PullRequest.Body:
Experimental prototype, opened as a draft so the work isn't lost. Not intended to merge as is.

## What

Behind `sessions.experimental.editorInAgentsWindow` (**on by default in this draft so it can be tried; must be off before merging**), **Open in Editor** in the Agents window no longer opens a separate window. It shows a real editor window for the session's folders *inside* the Agents window: the sessions list and the Agents title bar stay, and the editor replaces the area to the right of the list.

- Pressing the button again (now labelled **Back to Agents**), or selecting another session, shows the session again.
- The editor window stays loaded, so toggling back is instant and keeps tabs, splits and cursor.
- Each session remembers whether it showed its editor (persisted per window), so selecting it again, or restarting, restores it. Leaving the editor (Back to Agents, Open Agents Window from inside it, or closing it) forgets it.
- Sessions without folders still open a separate editor window, as before.

## How

- **Main process:** an embedded `CodeWindow` renders into a `WebContentsView` added to the Agents window and keeps a hidden `BrowserWindow` of its own for lifecycle, so close, quit, veto on dirty files and window restoration keep working. `ICodeWindow` gets `webContents`, `contentView`, `nativeWindow`, `embeddingWindow`, `embeddedWindows` and `layoutEmbedded`; main-process services that went through `win.webContents` now use `window.webContents` (`windowImpl.ts`, `windowsMainService.ts`, `lifecycleMainService.ts`, plus about a dozen call sites).
- **Native host:** `showEmbeddedEditorWindow`, `layoutEmbeddedEditorWindow`, `hideEmbeddedEditorWindow`.
- **Editor renderer:** an embedded flag hides its own title bar (`shouldShowCustomTitleBar`).
- **Agents renderer:** `src/vs/sessions/electron-browser/embeddedEditor.ts` toggles the editor, tracks its bounds (sidebar, resize, zoom), hides covered parts from keyboard/screen-reader navigation, swaps in a screenshot of the editor while Agents quick inputs/dialogs are open, and holds the per-session memory.

## Known gaps

- Agents notification toasts are hidden behind the editor.
- macOS menu commands reach the editor only while it has keyboard focus.
- Kept editor windows are only released when the Agents window closes.
- `LAYOUT.md` isn't updated yet.

## How to test

Launch Code OSS from this branch, open the Agents window, choose a folder for a session and click the VS Code icon in the title bar. Toggle back and forth, switch sessions, resize the window, toggle the sidebar, and restart.

Validation run:
- `pnpm run typecheck-client` — passed
- `pnpm run oxlint <changed files>` — passed
- `pnpm run valid-layers-check` — passed
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/test/electron-browser/embeddedEditor.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/test/electron-browser/vscodeActions.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/windows/test/electron-main/windowsFinder.test.ts` — 34 passing
- Manual run in a dev build (signed out): open, toggle back and forth, resize, sidebar toggle, closing the Agents window. Session switching and restore after restart are covered by unit tests only.

🤖 Authored with GitHub Copilot on behalf of @alexdima.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The last-session lookup reads startup-restored window state, createUntitledWorkspace generates a new config path, and windowsFinder matches multi-folder windows only by that path. The new session-selection autorun reaches this code on every return to a remembered session. This is static evidence; startup duration depends on workspace and extensions.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Untitled workspace files, full workbench renderers, workspace initialization, extension-host processes and file-watcher workers
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For R returns to the same remembered multi-folder session, there are R new workspace creations and R editor startups despite an unchanged folder set; local path validation is F stats per return for F folders. Workers are keyed by window ID, so duplicate editors do not share the per-window worker cache.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Repeated cold editor initialization delays session switching and accumulates duplicate renderer/process memory and workspace I/O.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Selecting another session and returning did not reopen an editor or create another workspace. Untitled workspace creation on the old explicit Open in Editor action existed, but was not performed on session-list navigation.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: For a session with multiple folders not matching a workspace from the previous application run, each return creates a new workspace config path. The existing embedded editor consequently misses the identity lookup and another complete editor is started instead of reusing it.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 338 creates a new untitled workspace before added line 349 searches embeddedWindows by workspaceUri. Added embeddedEditor.ts:255-258 invokes doShow again when a remembered session is selected, introducing this repeated creation into ordinary navigation.
Findings.Title: Reuse multi-folder editors before creating an untitled workspace
Findings.Impact: Open the embedded editor for a new two-folder session, switch to another session, then return repeatedly. Each return starts another editor and writes another untitled workspace rather than displaying the already-loaded editor, making navigation expensive even with a nominally warm cache.
Findings.Evidence: windowsMainService.ts:1259-1279 searches only doGetPathsFromLastSession(); :1186-1236 sources that list from windowsStateHandler.state. workspacesManagementMainService.ts:171-199 generates a new random config folder and performs mkdir/writeFile. windowsFinder.ts:42-58 matches workspace.configPath, not folder membership. windowsMainService.ts:349-357 therefore creates another CodeWindow; :1807 retains it. Each workbench loads normally (:1936), with window-keyed watcher workers (utilityProcessWorkerMainService.ts:80-84).
Findings.Recommendation: Match the current embedded editors by normalized folder set and remote authority before creating an untitled workspace, reusing their existing workspace identifier. Retain that identity for the embedded editor's lifetime and remove it on close; resolveLocalWorkspace already exposes workspace folders for comparison.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed hide path only hides the native view; the windows map and child view retain the full CodeWindow until an explicit editor close or parent close. Transitive worker ownership is per window and ends on close/reload, not hiding. The number of distinct workspaces visited and their memory footprints are unmeasured.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Hidden workbench renderer heaps and native views, local extension hosts, and per-window file-watcher workers
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Retention grows with the number of distinct workspace identities whose editors have been opened during one Agents-window lifetime, not with session count when folders are shared. Successful single-folder cache hits reuse one editor, but there is no cap or eviction across distinct folders/worktrees.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Growing resident memory and background process/watch activity persist after leaving editors, increasing memory pressure and reducing responsiveness during long-lived Agents sessions.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The editor was a separate, user-visible window with its ordinary close lifecycle. Closing it when returning to Agents released its workbench and window-bound processes; selecting sessions did not maintain an invisible editor cache owned by the Agents window.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Back to Agents and switching sessions leave every previously opened distinct workspace's complete editor resident, even when the session preference is forgotten. Only the visible-window map entry is removed; all hidden CodeWindows remain in the global windows map and attached to the parent.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 403 replaces the previous embedded editor with layoutEmbedded(undefined), whose added windowImpl.ts:1015-1024 only calls setVisible(false). No close or eviction occurs when Back to Agents forgets the session or when another workspace is opened.
Findings.Title: Bound retention of hidden embedded workbenches
Findings.Impact: A user opens editors for successive session folders/worktrees and presses Back to Agents after each. All those hidden workbenches and their window-owned resources remain loaded for the entire Agents-window lifetime, even though none is visible or remembered for automatic restoration.
Findings.Evidence: windowsMainService.ts:349-357 creates an editor for each missing workspace; :1807 stores it in windows. :399-403 deletes only visibleEmbeddedWindows and hides the previous view. windowImpl.ts:909-922 attaches its WebContentsView and closes it only during disposal; :1015-1024 does not dispose. EmbeddedEditorSessionMemory.willHide (:133-136) forgets the preference without releasing the editor. WorkspaceWatcher initializes recursive watches; UniversalWatcherClient creates a worker whose lifetime is close/reload, and utilityProcessWorkerMainService.ts:80-84 keys workers by windowId. Parent-close cleanup appears only at windowsMainService.ts:419-424.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep instant toggling for a bounded set of recently used embedded editors, but evict inactive clean editors through their normal close lifecycle and release editors for removed sessions. Preserve dirty-file vetoes/pinned editors rather than destroying them, and clear cache ownership on close.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: QuickAccess recreates its picker on provider changes; QuickInputController emits onShow for replacement without emitting its global onHide. The added handler unconditionally captures and the native service synchronously JPEG-encodes the full view before returning. Pixel size and measured encode latency are unknown, but redundant boundary calls and main-thread work are directly traced.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Full-view compositor readbacks, synchronous main-process JPEG encoding, image-byte IPC transfers and renderer Blob/image allocations
Findings.PerformanceScaling: One full-view capture and JPEG encode per picker onShow, including each provider change during a single continuously visible quick-input interval. Cost grows with provider replacements and captured pixel area; no snapshot reuse or in-flight coalescing exists, and native encoding runs on the single main-process thread.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Redundant main-thread CPU and image transfer/allocation work causes input latency and IPC contention, especially with a large or high-DPI editor view.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Quick-access provider replacement used the same quick-input surface without any native screenshot, JPEG encoding or image IPC transfer.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every quick-input controller replacement captures the embedded editor again, although the editor is already hidden behind the existing snapshot. Rapid replacements also launch independent captures and discard superseded results only after the expensive work.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 351 invokes getScreenshot for every onShow, even when picture already holds a snapshot or a previous request is in flight. The generation check at line 352 happens only after capture and encoding have completed.
Findings.Title: Reuse the snapshot while the editor is already occluded
Findings.Impact: With an embedded editor open, switch quick-access providers by changing the prefix, or replace an open picker with another picker. Each replacement repeats a full editor capture and JPEG(95) encode while the editor is already occluded; quick changes can produce captures whose results are immediately discarded.
Findings.Evidence: sessions.common.main.ts:38,265 enables the shared quick-access actions/providers. quickAccess.ts:213-224 recreates the picker when the provider changes and :166 calls show(). quickInputController.ts:742-757 replaces the old controller via didHide(), then :819 fires onShow; the service-level onHide fires only in hide() at :918. EmbeddedEditorService.occludeWhile (:348-352) has no picture/in-flight guard. nativeHostMainService.ts:1179-1184 calls capturePage(rect) with no rect here and synchronously toJPEG(95); embeddedEditor.ts:358-360 then copies the returned bytes into a Blob.
Findings.Recommendation: Capture once per actual occlusion interval and reuse its picture across picker replacements. Coalesce an in-flight capture rather than launching another; invalidate on embedded-window/bounds changes, and release the snapshot on the actual onHide or service-store disposal.

Scenarios.Scenario: First Open in Editor for a local or remote session; folderless/unsupported target fallback
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Target resolution is synchronous. The embedded show request awaits path validation, possible workspace construction, and profile/backup setup before showing the view. Renderer workbench initialization follows loadURL; extension initialization is needed for extension-backed editing, while watcher-worker creation is deferred until restore or a two-second timeout. Folderless targets retain the separate-window path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send one embedded-editor show request and return a visible-window notification.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One show call per requested editor display, not one per folder; one notification when the displayed editor changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One native openWindow request opened a separate editor for an explicit action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The show promise awaits main-process workspace/window setup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stat local folder paths and read previous-run workspace configs to locate a matching multi-root workspace.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: F stats for local input folders; for multi-root requests, validation of P prior entries plus workspace-config reads for matching candidates. Remote folder URI resolution has no stat.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Equivalent validation and previous-session matching occurred on explicit separate-window open; the new show path also uses them.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs before editor selection/creation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create the untitled workspace directory and serialize/write its config.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One mkdir and one config write for a multi-root request without a previous-run match.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old explicit multi-folder Open in Editor action also created an untitled workspace on this miss.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before creating the editor.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start local extension hosts and acquire a file-watcher utility worker for the loaded workbench.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Extension hosts per applicable running location; one watcher worker per window/module, not per workspace folder. WorkspaceWatcher groups recursive watch roots within that worker.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A separate editor initialized the same workbench-owned resources on first open.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Extension initialization affects extension features; watcher creation is deferred past renderer restoration.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve remote authority and establish management/remote extension-host connections when opening a remote workbench.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Connections per remote workbench/service and applicable remote extension host, not per folder; persistent connections are reused within that workbench.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The separate remote editor used the same connection initialization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Remote connection/initialization gates remote file and extension functionality.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Construct the hidden lifecycle BrowserWindow in addition to the WebContentsView that loads the workbench.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One hidden native window plus one workbench view per new embedded editor.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One visible BrowserWindow hosted the editor directly.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Native objects are constructed during the show request.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: F session folders, generally one or a small multi-root set; P previous-run windows examined for a multi-folder request; one newly created editor on a genuine cache miss.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Local folder stats run through Promise.all. Previous-run path validation is parallel, then candidate workspace-file reads are sequential. Editor creation requests have no shared limiter or in-flight coalescer. Within a created renderer, extension start is asynchronous and watcher workers are owned per window/module.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Single-folder editors are looked up by normalized folder URI among this parent's embedded windows. A cold miss loads a workbench; a warm hit reuses it but still validates local paths. Remote URI normalization performs no filesystem/network lookup itself. Resolver extraction preserves previous resource-conversion behavior. Multi-folder cache identity is defective as analyzed separately.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the traced boundaries and their grouping; no independent first-use regression is reported beyond the retention/reuse issues below.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No runtime measurements; startup and remote-connection cost depend on installed extensions, workspace size and network. First-use initialization is largely the intended substitution for a separate editor.
Scenarios.Verdict: First-use loading and resolver extraction are behavior-equivalent in expensive subsystem work. Folderless fallback adds no reportable performance mechanism.

Scenarios.Scenario: Re-select a remembered session, including restoration after restart and repeated multi-folder navigation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The AfterRestored contribution instantiates the service, which waits for initial session restore and known folders. Only the active remembered session is shown, not all remembered sessions. On later selection, native show setup and any new workbench initialization precede a usable restored editor.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Revalidate folder/prior-run paths, reread workspace configs, then create another untitled workspace.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: F local stats and prior-run validation/matching per show; one mkdir/write per return on the unchanged prior-run miss. R returns create R workspaces rather than using one cached identity.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Selecting another session and returning performed no editor-open workspace I/O. Comparable work ran only on the old explicit Open in Editor action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All workspace resolution/creation is awaited before display setup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load another complete editor and start its workbench-owned extension/watcher resources after the cache miss.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One new editor per return in the multi-folder miss scenario; watcher workers are keyed by the new window ID and do not deduplicate across duplicates.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Session navigation did not start editors or their workers; an already-open separate editor remained independently available.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Repeated renderer initialization gates editing; watcher startup is deferred but still consumes resources.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Initialize persistent remote connections in each newly created remote editor.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Per duplicate remote workbench, not per folder; within-workbench connection caching does not reuse the prior editor instance.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No additional remote workbench connections were created by session selection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Remote editor readiness depends on connection initialization.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize remembered session IDs through the storage service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Only on additions/removals/identity migration, not every selection; proportional to remembered-ID count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No embedded-editor preference existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Small synchronous preference update before show; actual storage persistence is service-managed.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: R returns to the same session; F folders; P previous-run window entries. A two-folder session absent from prior-run state is enough to trigger repeated editor creation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One automatic show for the initially selected remembered session. Selection autoruns fire-and-forget show requests without a sequencer/limiter. Each multi-folder show performs parallel path validation, sequential workspace matching, then independent editor creation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Startup memory stores session IDs, not editor objects; there is no renderer cache across restart. Within the same run, single-folder hits reuse one editor. Multi-folder requests consult only prior-run state, create a fresh untitled config on every miss, then search by that fresh config URI, so even a previously loaded editor is missed. Empty/failed previous-run matches are not negatively cached.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the startup-state source, fresh config-path generation, config-URI window matching and new selection caller are all traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Prevalence of multi-root sessions is unknown. The repeated cold startup and duplicate allocation are established without relying on a large folder count or measured timing. Session-ID storage alone is not treated as a meaningful regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported the broken multi-folder cache identity. Automatic restoration of only one selected session is intentional and does not fan out over all stored sessions.

Scenarios.Scenario: Back to Agents and browsing editors for many distinct session folders/worktrees in a long-lived window
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Hiding sends one native request and changes native view visibility. Returning to Agents does not wait for editor shutdown because no shutdown is attempted; retained editors continue owning their workbench resources.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Hide the editor and notify the parent renderer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One hide request/visibility notification per transition; no lifecycle unload IPC occurs on hide.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The separate editor could be closed through its ordinary lifecycle when returning to Agents.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Fast transition to Agents; does not release editor resources.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Retain hidden workbenches and their extension/watcher processes rather than unloading them.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to W loaded workbenches and their per-window resources; shared folder/session keys reduce W but do not bound it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Closing a separate editor ended its window-bound resources; no invisible cache was automatically owned by the Agents window.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the immediate hide critical path, but retained resources compete with ongoing work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Keep recursive workspace watch subscriptions alive after editors are hidden.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Deduplicated roots within each workbench; per-window worker ownership persists across W retained editors.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Subscriptions were released when the separate editor was closed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Background activity and watch events can continue after the user leaves the editor.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Retain persistent remote-workbench connections in hidden editors.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Per retained remote workbench/service, not per session or folder when editors are shared.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Closing the separate remote editor disposed its workbench-owned connections.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Background connection/resource retention; not awaited by hide.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: W distinct workspace identities opened during one parent-window lifetime. Sessions sharing a single folder reuse one editor and are not counted separately.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One visible editor at a time, but W hidden/visible workbenches may simultaneously own extension hosts, watcher workers and remote connections. Worker deduplication is per window/module, not across W workspaces. Hiding only disposes renderer layout/screenshot listeners for the current editor.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A successful single-folder cache is unbounded across distinct workspace identities. Back to Agents forgets the automatic-show preference but leaves the cached editor resident. There is no TTL/LRU/session-removal eviction; actual editor close or parent close releases it.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: windows-map retention, native child-view ownership and close-only disposal are explicit; hide performs setVisible(false) only.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Distinct-workspace visitation rate, extension footprint and parent-window lifetime are unmeasured. The resource lifecycle and unbounded distinct-key scaling are directly established.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported unbounded hidden-workbench retention independently of the duplicate multi-folder cache miss.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resize, sidebar visibility/width changes and zoom while an embedded editor is visible
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The Agents renderer computes editor geometry on the next animation frame and sends bounds to main, which updates one native view. Layout must propagate before the embedded editor matches the new geometry.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Transfer one bounds object to the main process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one call per scheduled animation frame for all coalesced resize/layout/zoom signals.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Separate editor windows handled their own native/renderer layout without this parent-to-view layout request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required to update native editor geometry; scheduled rather than synchronous event-by-event.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read a fixed number of DOM bounds/computed styles, then set the visible native view's bounds and border radius.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A fixed number of geometry/style reads and one native bounds update per coalesced frame, independent of session/cache size.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No embedded-view geometry synchronization was required.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs on renderer/main UI threads for resizing.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Layout/resize events and animation frames; one currently visible editor regardless of W cached editors.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: At most one pending animation-frame layout callback per visible-editor subscription. Native layout operations are serialized by the main-process event loop; there is no per-cached-editor fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The last bounds are stored once per parent. Pending layout uses MutableDisposable to coalesce multiple events into one scheduled frame. Listener/observer ownership is disposed on visible-editor change; there is no per-hidden-editor resize subscription.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in event coalescing, constant cardinality and disposal ownership.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No profiling of style-resolution/native-layout time. The diff shows fixed-size reads and explicit frame coalescing, not an established scaling or repeated-relayout defect.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate reportable layout regression established; do not infer forced-layout pathology from getBoundingClientRect alone.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agents quick inputs/dialogs above an embedded editor, including quick-access provider replacements
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Initial browser-overlay visibility above the native view waits for capturePage, main-process JPEG encoding, returned image bytes, then an occlusion update scheduled for the next frame. Provider replacement in a continuously visible picker is already covered by a snapshot but unconditionally repeats capture. Native dialogs follow their existing platform-dialog path and also trigger the generic new capture listener.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request a full embedded-workbench screenshot and return encoded image bytes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One round trip per onShow, including each quick-access provider replacement; no per-folder/session multiplicity.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Agents quick-input/provider transitions did not capture an editor or transfer image bytes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initial occlusion waits for the response; repeated requests unnecessarily compete with UI/main IPC.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Compositor capturePage of the full view followed by synchronous NativeImage.toJPEG(95).
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: T full-view readbacks/encodes; cost proportional to D, with no cropped rect supplied.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The screenshot service existed for explicit screenshot features, not on Agents quick-input show/provider transitions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Readback precedes returning the screenshot, and JPEG encoding occupies the shared main-process thread.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Copy screenshot bytes into a Blob, create an object URL and decode/display an image.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per non-superseded successful capture; superseded captures still incurred native encoding/IPC but skip this allocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No placeholder image allocations occurred on quick-input transitions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Creates the placeholder before occluding the native view.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Show a native confirmation/prompt via electron.dialog when custom dialogs are not selected.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One native dialog operation per processed dialog; dialog model serializes its queue.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same native/custom dialog routing and queued processing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: User response determines dialog completion; the new screenshot is not required to bring a native dialog above views.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: T quick-input onShow events, including provider changes without global onHide; D physical pixels in the editor view; dialog events. Ordinary keystrokes within the same provider do not each capture.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Multiple onShow handlers can have asynchronous captures in flight. Native JPEG encoding runs serially on the main-process thread. Layout requests are frame-coalesced but screenshot requests are not. Quick-input and dialog listeners own separate pictures, with no shared capture coordinator.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The picture is retained until actual onHide, but onShow does not reuse it. Generation invalidation discards late results only after capture/encoding; no in-flight coalescing exists. Picture URLs/images are revoked/removed through MutableDisposable and store disposal, so this is repeated work rather than an unbounded image leak.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: provider changes recreate and show a picker; controller replacement emits onShow without service-level onHide; the new capture lacks picture/in-flight guards.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual screenshot/encode duration depends on view size, DPI and hardware. The repeated provider-change trigger and full-view synchronous encode are proven; no benchmark timings claimed.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported redundant captures during a continuing occlusion interval, not the intentional first snapshot or correctness of overlay visibility.

Scenarios.Scenario: Close the Agents parent, close an embedded editor, quit and restore window state
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Normal parent close asks ready embedded renderers for vetoes before the parent, then awaits their unload work before closing native windows. Dirty-file decisions intentionally serialize. During app quit, embedded-parent aggregation is skipped and the existing per-window quit path applies. State persistence excludes embedded editors.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request renderer veto and unload completion over dedicated IPC reply channels.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: For successful normal parent close, two request/reply exchanges per ready candidate, N+1 candidates; veto stops the first phase early. Quit does not aggregate children into the parent list.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Closing the Agents window sent these two lifecycle exchanges only to its own renderer; separately opened editors remained independent. App quit already processed each opened window.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All applicable replies and cleanup precede parent close; serial ordering preserves dirty-file veto behavior.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Close/destroy child lifecycle windows and dispose their workbench views.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One close/disposal per remaining embedded editor; visibility and bounds maps have one entry per parent and are removed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Separate editors had their own ordinary close lifecycle.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Part of parent shutdown; releases the retained native/renderer resources.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist top-level restoration state through the existing state service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Embedded windows are filtered out; state entries scale with top-level windows rather than N children.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: All ordinary editor windows were eligible for restoration-state persistence.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing persistence/shutdown behavior; avoids restoring hidden lifecycle windows as standalone editors.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N ready embedded editors in one parent; includes only effective retained workspace/window instances, not all stored session preferences.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: On normal parent close, before-unload requests are sequential across N children plus parent, followed by sequential will-unload requests. Quit uses ordinary separate-window close handling. No repeated per-window unload is introduced where a pending unload promise is reused.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Unload promises are coalesced per window ID. Parent close deletes visibility/bounds state and destroys any remaining child lifecycle windows; CodeWindow disposal closes the workbench WebContentsView. No editor restoration fan-out from top-level window-state persistence.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in sequential lifecycle cardinality, per-window unload coalescing and view cleanup ownership.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Renderer cleanup time and dirty-file prevalence are unmeasured. N can grow due to reported retention problems, but mandatory veto/cleanup ordering is not independently reported as a regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: Close/quit cleanup is present and preserves required veto semantics. Additional close cost is a consequence of retained editors, not a separate generic unnecessary-await finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Main-process routing for menus, browser views, authentication, diagnostics, profiling and utility-process ports
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Commands and service responses target the workbench WebContents rather than the parent/native lifecycle window. Existing dialog/network/diagnostic/profiling operations remain on their prior workflow paths. Embedded WebContents lookup may scan the windows collection after the normal direct lookup fails.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Transfer existing message ports or execute workbench/webview operations against the correct WebContents.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Same port/operation count per existing request; no extra subprocess created by the routing substitutions themselves.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Used responseWindow.win.webContents; now uses responseWindow.webContents.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing utility-process connection and service operations depend on delivery.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Present credentials through the focused renderer and resolve proxy through its Electron session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing proxy request/auth grouping is unchanged; richer window ownership does not itself add network calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Used the BrowserWindow's WebContents/session instead of the workbench-owned WebContents.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Credentials/proxy resolution can gate requests as before.
